A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 11-page DC-TTA paper, with readable text, equations, figures, and tables. All supplied pages support comparison. Neither PDF includes the supplementary material referenced in the text, so that external material cannot be assessed.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, and experiments applying DC-TTA to conventional interactive segmentation methods in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original quantitative experiments in Tables 1–3 and qualitative segmentation results in Figures 5–7.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical click assignment, segmentation units, adaptation losses, mask aggregation, task-vector merging, and final refinement procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight benchmarks: CAMO, COD10K, TRASHCAN, ISTD, Berkeley, DAVIS, COCOMVal, and PascalVOC. The represented tasks and domains are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains SAM, TENT, AdaptSAM, and DC-only comparisons. Table 3 retains the same RITM, FocalClick, and MFP comparisons with and without DC-TTA.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains identical dataset counts, instance handling, simulated-click placement, NoC/FR metrics, 20-click budget, and model settings. Tables 1–3 use unchanged evaluation conditions.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains identical ablations of naive TTA, divide-and-conquer processing, and model merging. The qualitative comparisons and segmentation-unit analysis in Figures 3 and 5–7 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and qualitative results match. For example, Table 1 reports DC-TTA CAMO NoC90 of 9.58 and FR90 of 25.60 in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations (1)–(22) are identical, including the losses, unit updates, mask union, and model-merging formulation. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about partitioning clicks, localized adaptation, model merging, and improved interactive segmentation over SAM and conventional TTA.

C2.justification: The explanations of conflicting click signals, localized specialization, and integration of adapted knowledge are unchanged. No substantive interpretation, applicability qualification, or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: Both retain SAM ViT-B, 1024×1024 inputs, one AdamW update of the prompt encoder and mask decoder, learning rate 1e-5, and merging scale 0.7. Both still state that code will be available soon.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 62 reference entries are identical. Positioning relative to interactive segmentation, TTA, and model-merging research is unchanged.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 29 June 2025 to v2 dated 14 April 2026. The paper's wording, author block, headings, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7, Tables 1–3, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages match apart from the updated version/date text in the first-page margin.

improvement.justification: The supplied versions contain identical scientific content, experimental evidence, explanations, and displays. Updating the arXiv stamp does not improve or diminish the paper's scientific support, clarity, or reproducibility.
